prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: a single high-fidelity visual direction comp for a native iOS rail departures app
Primary request: Design one complete, shippable-looking portrait iPhone app screen for Last Train. Reconstruct the visual logic of a 1970s British pocket timetable as a genuinely ultra-modern interface: a raked rack of tinted glass timetable slides seated on a softly lit goldenrod bed. This must read as a contemporary native iOS operating screen, never as a marketing poster or nostalgic print reproduction.
Scene/backdrop: Full-bleed 393x852-style iPhone app screen with no phone hardware frame. Reserve clean safe space for the Dynamic Island at the top. The interface occupies the entire image edge to edge.
Subject and layout: A calm goldenrod application canvas. At the top, a precise mode control visibly includes "LAST TRAIN" and "FAST TRAIN". Make LAST TRAIN the active mode. Below it, show "Upminster" as the origin and "EAST" as a compact direction cell. Make the primary result "23:47" with destination "Shoeburyness"; use red only here to communicate the actual last train. Beneath, create exactly three crisp, precisely angled departure strips in a raked rack, showing "22:58", "23:18", and "23:32". At the lower part of the screen show "FIRST BACK 05:12" and the quiet note "Direct services only".
Style/medium: high-fidelity shippable native iOS UI mockup, sophisticated editorial transport information design, tactility expressed through modern glass and light rather than skeuomorphic decoration.
Typography: one consistent condensed sans-serif type size across the information system; create hierarchy only through weight, uppercase/lowercase, dark/light reversal, and fixed timetable cells. All supplied copy must be sharp, correctly spelled, and immediately readable.
Color palette: #E8AD1A goldenrod canvas and light bed, #172025 deep slate, #F2E7CC warm ivory, #245746 bottle green. Use #B92F26 red exclusively for the primary last-train result; no red elsewhere.
Materials/textures: thin tinted glass or scratched acetate departure strips, faint ruler registration lines and restrained micro-scratches, precise highlights, controlled depth, tactile but clean. The rack angles should feel engineered, not chaotic.
Composition/framing: portrait 393x852 proportions, generous iOS safe areas, strong scan path from mode to origin to primary time to three recent departures to first return. Align type to a strict grid. Make all controls feel tappable and reachable. No bottom tab bar.
Text (verbatim, render every item exactly once and do not add misspellings): "LAST TRAIN", "FAST TRAIN", "Upminster", "EAST", "23:47", "Shoeburyness", "22:58", "23:18", "23:32", "FIRST BACK 05:12", "Direct services only"
Constraints: exactly three angled departure strips; one consistent condensed type size; hierarchy via weight, case, reversal, and fixed cells; safe Dynamic Island space; immediately scannable train times; contemporary native iOS screen.
Avoid: phone hardware frame, hands, device mockup, marketing poster, promotional headline, generic rounded cards, floating card grid, bottom tab bar, gradients unrelated to real material lighting, glassmorphism blobs, neon cyberpunk styling, retro illustration, generic dashboard widgets, durations, journey lengths, "+1", next-day labels, calendar dates, extra navigation labels, extra train times, illegible or invented text, red used anywhere except the last-train result.
